scope: NativeScene apply_update/apply_patches transactionality: apply the ordered frame atomically to a retained source Scene clone, build a detached native candidate from that terminal source, restore host-visible state, and swap only after both stages succeed.

behavior.rejected_native_candidate: Source snapshot, active native document, version, focus, viewport scroll, pointer hover/press, frame cache and pixels remain unchanged.
behavior.accepted_frame: One candidate document becomes active; focus, grouped scroll, hover, native press identity and prior frame/damage cache are restored; scene version equals the exact admitted successor.
behavior.semantic_tag_change: A legal Button to non-Button source semantic update is rebuilt with the correct native element instead of rejecting the whole frame.

checks: zero-font-size native candidate rejected after the source Scene batch accepted

a later valid frame from the retained old expected version succeeded

integration_evidence.test_suite: GPU damage regression after candidate rebuilding
integration_evidence.result: native_gpu_frame_damage 3/3 and native_gpu_render 3/3 passed; candidate carries the previous frame so local damage remains local

limitations: The retained source Scene clone must stay the authoritative engine snapshot; direct external mutation of a separately held Scene is not observed without an admitted update.
The implementation rebuilds the full native candidate for each accepted frame. This is a correctness checkpoint, not a performance baseline or optimization.
Native construction uses third-party APIs that may fail or panic; false is returned for observed failure, while third-party panic rollback is not claimed.
Checklist item 2 remains incomplete because the full ordered proof and actual display/window presentation remain open.
